articles.title: Chris Paul Jokes About Clippers Exit in Video Amid Aaron Rodgers' Steelers Benching
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers' situation with the Pittsburgh Steelers brought back memories for Chris Paul and the end of his NBA career with the Los Angeles Clippers.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers' situation with the Pittsburgh Steelers brought back memories for Chris Paul and the end of his NBA career with the Los Angeles Clippers.

Appearing on The Pat McAfee Show , Paul jokingly asked "did you see what happened to me last year" when Pat McAfee asked if he could recall a situation like Rodgers' happening in the NBA.

The Pittsburgh Steelers, in a surprise move, announced late Tuesday night that would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos and Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback.

It was a situation that seemed to come out of nowhere since as recently as Monday Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters Rodgers was going to be the starter going forward.

Paul's final NBA season in 2025-26 came to an abrupt end when the Clippers announced they were parting ways with the franchise icon reportedly due to clashes with various people in the organization, including management, head coach Tyronn Lue and other players.

The Clippers were able to trade Paul to the Toronto Raptors prior to the trade deadline, but he was waived by the club and subsequently announced his retirement.

Rodgers has said in no uncertain terms this is his final year in the NFL. There's no indication at this point that Pittsburgh will keep him sidelined for the remainder of the season, but the abrupt nature of the quarterback change at least opens up the possibility that Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles was his last game.

The Steelers (6-4) are currently in the final playoff spot in the AFC. They have lost their last two games coming out of a Week 9 bye and will look to avoid their first three-game losing streak since the 2024 season against the Broncos on Friday.

articles.title: Kevin Porter Jr., Magic Agree to Contract in NBA Free Agency After Bucks Stint
articles.summary: Free agent guard Kevin Porter Jr. is reportedly headed to the Orlando Magic after getting waived by the Milwaukee Bucks ahead of the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Free agent guard Kevin Porter Jr. is reportedly headed to the Orlando Magic after getting waived by the Milwaukee Bucks ahead of the 2026-27 season.

Porter is finalizing a two-year with the Magic, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

He also met with the Denver Nuggets before working out his deal with the Magic, per Charania.

Porter averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 2.2 steals per game in 38 appearances with the Bucks last season. He missed most of the campaign with a right knee injury that necessitated surgery.

Marc Stein first reported Monday that Porter was meeting with the Magic. Porter will now slot into the 15th remaining standard contract spot on the Magic's roster, per the Orlando Sentinel 's Jason Beede .

The Denver Post 's Bennett Durando reported the Nuggets had been in contact with Porter, but added the team "wanted to slow-play any potential roster moves and let the season develop first."

NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer had also previously connected the Sacramento Kings , Miami Heat and Portland Trail Blazers to an interest in Porter.

Porter has previous experience playing professionally in Greece. Stein reported earlier Wednesday Porter was leaning toward staying in the NBA "even if he has to take a minimum-salary deal... rather than returning to Europe on more lucrative terms."

The Magic are off to a 7-10 start to the season with a backcourt led by Jalen Suggs and Anthony Black.

Porter could now join Desmond Bane as another member of the Magic's guard rotation as the team looks to bounce back from dropping three of their last four games.

The Magic were $10.2 million over the first apron and $2.5 million under teh second apron before signing Porter, according to Spotrac .

Orlando has about $29 million in first-apron space and $41.9 million in second apron space next season with Franz Wagner, Paolo Banchero, Bane and Suggs already under contract. Anthony Black is currently a pending restricted free agent.

The Athletic's Sam Amick reported earlier this month "the notion of Orlando breaking up its core (outside of Black) if the Magic fall short of expectations again is clearly in play."

"The internal focus now — from the front office to first-year coach Sean Sweeney on down — is on making the most of this current roster and taking it from there," Amick reported.

Porter said in September he felt "100 percent" after undergoing the second of two knee procedures in July, per the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel 's Jim Owczarski . His health and conditioning could influence how quickly he joins the Magic, which are next in action Saturday at the Washington Wizards.

articles.title: Chus Mateo: "Hay que cuidar a estos chicos, son superhéroes"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador valora el esfuerzo de los internacionales que jugaron el martes la Euroliga y destaca la importancia del Montenegro-España: "Ahora cualquier victoria es decisiva"
articles.summary: El seleccionador valora el esfuerzo de los internacionales que jugaron el martes la Euroliga y destaca la importancia del Montenegro-España: "Ahora cualquier victoria es decisiva"
articles.body: Chus Mateo lo ve claro. Antes del primer y último entrenamiento de la selección en Podgorica (mañana habrá sesión de tiro), el seleccionador nacional advirtió de que en estos dos partidos España puede certificar su clasificación. No convienen titubeos. De ahí su convocatoria con jugadores que disputan la Euroliga y la necesidad de cuidarles. "Son extraordinarios estos chicos. Ponen mucho de su parte. Quieren ser parte de esta clasificación. Quieren dar todo lo que tienen. Su compromiso es máximo. Hay que cuidarles porque juegan Liga Endesa, Euroliga y ahora la selección. Son superhéroes". Por primera vez en la semana, Mateo pudo contar con el grueso de los jugadores que citó el 13 de noviembre. Parra, Brizuela, Cárdenas, Saint Supéry y Juancho se han incorporado sin problemas y todos estarán este jueves (19.00 h., TDP) ante Montenegro, en busca de la sexta victoria en el grupo de clasificación. La lógica dice que Qatar 2027 está en alcanzar siete. El seleccionador habló de la complejidad en la preparación de este encuentro. "Con estos jugadores que vinieron hoy hay que ser muy sintéticos. No vamos a hacer un entrenamiento de mucha carga. Hay que priorizar lo importante. Saben que hay que sacar el partido como sea. Y están responsabilizados". Mateo, serio, trato de comunicar la importancia del partido de Podgorica ante la colista del grupo de España. "Tenemos claro que es importante para nosotros. Ahora cualquier victoria nos acerca al Mundial. Hay que afrontarlo con responsabilidad. La afición animará mucho. Sabiendo que ellos van a poner mucha energía. Tenemos que jugar bien al baloncesto, entender por dónde van los tiros, saber lo que nos espera. Montenegro juega bien en casa. Hay que saberlo. Es importante entender dónde jugamos, seguramente no ganas con un baloncesto de alta calidad. Ganas con más deseo, con más esfuerzo. Seguro que el deseo, las ganas y la energía son claves para el triunfo", comentó antes del entrenamiento de la selección.

articles.title: LSU wins court round as SEC's nuclear option could carry a $1 billion price tag, while RJ Luis sues Sankey
articles.summary: RJ Luis seeks damages from the SEC in an amended complaint, with attorney Tony Clayton warning Greg Sankey will "feel the wrath" as Bayou Gumbo simmers.
articles.body: The gumbo is simmering between the SEC and LSU as the two sides squared-off in federal court Wednesday morning, while another lawsuit in Baton Rouge was amended to include commissioner Greg Sankey. The ongoing saga with these two has become one of the main storylines to follow in college athletics over the past four months, thanks to eligibility fights centered around former athletes with professional experience. What started with Lane Kiffin hoping to roster Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris in September has now bled into the Tigers shenanigans with basketball player RJ Luis over the past month. LANE KIFFIN’S ROSTER FIGHT SET THE STAGE, WILL WADE JUST THREW A GRENADE IN LSU-SEC WAR WITH RJ LUIS When LSU decided it would allow Luis to play last week, this set off a chain of events that has now led to the SEC preparing to hold a meeting next week to decide LSU's future in the conference. SEC is not protected by the legal system, while LSU can sue if expelled On Wednesday in a Alabama federal court, the SEC and LSU squared-off over a TRO and Preliminary injunction the conference was seeking that would allow them to enforce their rules immediately ahead of the December 3rd meeting. Judge Annemarie Axon denied the SEC's request for the TRO on all four counts that were presented to the court from conference lawyers. This also means that LSU will be allowed to sue the conference if it decides to actually terminate the Tigers, which would now not be protected by a federal court. This is obviously a win for LSU, under the circumstances both sides are dealing with. The judge made it a point to say she was not going to stop others like LSU from being allowed to file lawsuits, which would infringe upon their first amendment rights. In essence, a federal court is not protecting the SEC right now from any lawsuits by LSU if conference presidents decided to vote them out. BRUCE PEARL JOINS DAN DAKICH TO WEIGH IN ON MESSY LSU SITUATION: 'GO TO ANOTHER LEAGUE' If the SEC did decide to vote LSU out, Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill noted that the state would have no other choice but to sue the Southeastern Conference for what she said could be a $1 billion lawsuit. Will the SEC move ahead with its meeting next week to discuss kicking LSU out of the conference? As of Wednesday, sources tell OutKick this is the case. But, the judge did not rule on LSU's motion to dismiss the lawsuit all together. RJ Luis files amended complaint seeking damages against SEC "The conference and Sankey acted with actual malice, out of spite and ill will toward Mr. Luis, without any legitimate interest. No rule of the Conference supplied a basis for any penalty against LSU on account of Mr. Luis. They singled him out." If you have been paying attention, this has been the plan all along. Once RJ Luis was denied the opportunity to continue playing college basketball, he was going to sue the SEC for monetary damages in court. This has also been the thinking of many within the legal field around Baton Rouge over the past few months, along with the two football players who were not rostered by LSU in September. SEC ACCUSES LSU OF DEFYING ITS RULES AS WILL WADE’S BASKETBALL ROSTER ADDS FUEL TO A BURNING FIRE Now, attorney Tony Clayton is trying to get SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey and conference Presidents deposed over what transpired over the month prior that has led to a contentious back-and-forth between the two parties. "Mr. Sankey ought to be put on notice that he will see what we're about to do because of his actions and Mr. Sankey will feel the wrath of RJ Luis, if not by Christmas, then by New Year's night," Attorney Tony Clayton said to ESPN this week. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If the complaint is amended by the court, this will put the SEC as a whole in the crosshairs of the same Baton Rouge court that has ruled against them multiple times over the past few months. And, if this were to get to the discovery phase, the ramifications could end up being pretty significant if every person who was involved in these conversations over eligibility were deposed under oath. Does it actually get that far? Well, that's going to depend on whether the SEC and LSU can come to some sort of an agreement on what both sides are willing to give. Just when you thought it would be a cordial holiday season between all parties involved, two cases in two different states have provided more drama than an afternoon Thanksgiving lunch at your crazy aunt's house. There are going to be some awkward conversations over the next few days.

articles.title: No. 2 Virginia and Marquette get a nearly 2-hour halftime thanks to ... an indoor rain delay?
articles.summary: Feast Week chaos: an indoor rain delay at the Battle 4 Atlantis pushed No. 2 Virginia's halftime to nearly two hours and Texas A&M and Xavier's tip back.
articles.body: One of the great things about Feast Week is that you can turn on ESPN at noon on a Wednesday and watch No. 2 Virginia play Marquette in the Bahamas. Weather permitting, apparently. COLLEGE BASKETBALL GETS A NEW NO. 1 AS THREE TEAMS FALL OUT OF THE AP TOP FIVE IN A SINGLE WEEK The Cavaliers took a 25-23 lead into halftime of Wednesday’s opener at the men’s Battle 4 Atlantis. If you tuned in expecting to catch the start of the second half, you got to watch arena workers furiously trying to dry the floor. There were towels spread out right on top of the logo at center court. A leak in the roof at Imperial Arena had given us an honest-to-goodness indoor rain delay. At 1:30 p.m. ET, ESPN reported there was no timetable for play to resume. The teams finally got the second half underway around 2:45 p.m. ET. That made for a halftime of about an hour and 50 minutes, roughly 95 minutes longer than usual. UPDATE: Once the floor dried, No. 2 Virginia beat Marquette 60-54 to improve to 8-0. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Normally when I hear there’s no timetable to resume, I pull up the radar to see whether I’m going to get to watch the rest of a baseball game. It never occurred to me to check the forecast before settling in for some Virginia basketball. Although, in fairness to Atlantis, the resort does advertise a 141-acre water park. I just assumed the basketball court was somewhere on the property where you could safely leave your towel in the room. Texas A&M and Xavier were supposed to tip off on that same floor at 2:30. That time came and went before Virginia and Marquette even started the second half. The Aggies and Musketeers were looking at a 4:15 p.m. ET start, an hour and 45 minutes later than scheduled. And the folks at Atlantis still had Memphis–Penn State on the books for 5 and Wake Forest–Mississippi State at 7:30. Four games on one court, and they made it through exactly one half before the whole day got thrown off. How’s that for a start to the tournament? The best part? There’s an argument to be made that this wasn’t even the strangest delay Virginia had this month. Back on Nov. 8, the Cavaliers were two minutes away from beating Arkansas in Washington, D.C., when a pair of pigeons landed on the court. Arkansas coach John Calipari himself helped chase them off so the teams could finish the game. Remind me again what these guys are getting out of playing indoors?

articles.title: NBA announces 10bn euro fund for European arenas as part of plans for new continental league
articles.summary: The NBA steps up its plans for a European league by announcing a strategy to invest at least 10bn euros in the development of basketball arenas across the continent.
articles.body:
The NBA has stepped up its plans for a European league by announcing a strategy to invest at least 10bn euros in the development and renovation of basketball arenas across the continent.

The league has assembled a group of investment firms for the project, which would also look to improve the sports and entertainment districts around the arenas.

The initiative forms part of the NBA and the International Basketball Federation's (Fiba) plan to launch a new, professional basketball system in Europe in 2027.

It will provide prospective clubs and ownership groups with access to capital and the NBA's expertise in regard to developing modern arenas and their surroundings.

"We've seen first-hand how state-of-the-art arenas and the related developments around them can transform basketball teams and their surrounding communities," said NBA commissioner Adam Silver.

"As we prepare to launch a new league in Europe alongside Fiba, we see a significant opportunity to help clubs develop facilities which both build on the unique traditions that define European basketball while also elevating the fan experience and attracting many more live events."

The NBA's announcement stated that the plans for the areas surrounding arenas could include housing, workplaces, restaurants, retail and public spaces, ensuring they would be year-round destinations.

In the statement, the investors said: "We're excited to work with the NBA to support a transformative phase of infrastructure development across Europe.

"Together, we have the potential to invest billions of euros to create world-class venues in European cities, honouring the passion and traditions of European basketball fans and supporting lasting economic growth in the communities where the game means so much."

The announcement cited a study by The Sports Consultancy, which claimed the NBA and Fiba's league could contribute more than 24bn euros in gross value added to GDP across Europe.

It also claimed the league could support nearly 15,000 full-time equivalent jobs annually and attract nearly 70 million spectators over its first 10 years.

articles.title: Joel Embiid downgraded to out for 76ers' NBA Cup matchup vs. Miami Heat on Wednesday due to illness
articles.summary: Embiid will miss his second consecutive game due to illness and will have sat out five of the 76ers' 18 games this season.
articles.body:
Joel Embiid was listed as doubtful due to illness for Wednesday's NBA Cup matchup between the Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat . Before the game, the Philadelphia center was downgraded to out, per The Athletic's Tony Jones .

Embiid also missed Monday's 128-111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers . The Sixers center will have missed five of the team's 18 games this season.

Prior to Monday, he had appeared in Philadelphia's past three games and played arguably his best basketball of the season, averaging 30 points. That stretch includes Saturday's 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks during which he nearly notched a triple-double with 26 points, 17 rebounds and 9 assists.

Embiid was involved in a crucial play in the closing seconds , taking an inbounds pass from LeBron James and stepping out of bounds at the baseline. However, the officials failed to notice Embiid's left foot going out and the Bucks were out of replay challenges to contest the call.

Embiid is the 76ers' third-leading scorer at 20.4 points per game while leading the team with 8.9 rebounds. His 4.1 assists rank fourth among Sixers players.

The 76ers currently have the top record in the Eastern Conference at 14-4 and are tied for second in the NBA behind the 15-3 San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers. Philadelphia has won seven of its past 10 games.

Following Wednesday's contest, the Sixers have back-to-back games on the road, visiting the Indiana Pacers (6-12) on Friday and facing the Houston Rockets (13-5) on Saturday.

Embiid seems likely to miss at least one of those games—either due to illness or to manage his right foot plantar fascia, which sidelined him for a game when the Sixers played a back-to-back.

Head coach Nick Nurse added on Wednesday that they did not know yet whether Embiid would be traveling with the team to Indiana.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Attends LeBron James, 76ers vs. Giannis, Heat After Visiting UPenn Basketball Team
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark has had a busy few days in Philadelphia.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark has had a busy few days in Philadelphia.

Clark visited the Penn men's basketball team before attending Wednesday afternoon's game between the Miami Heat and Philadelphia 76ers, per NBC Sports' John Clark and The Philly Voice's Adam Aaronson .

Clark, whose boyfriend Connor McCaffery is the son of Penn head coach son of Fran McCaffery, has already been in attendance for both Sixers and Quakers games this season.

The Fever star talked with LeBron James and met Tyrese Maxey for the first time after sitting courtside for an Oct. 28 game between the Sixers and the host Indiana Pacers.

She and Connor McCaffery were also spotted sitting behind the Penn bench during a Nov. 5 game at Illinois.

Clark was again in attendance Tuesday night for Penn's 89-74 win over Drexel, per Conor Smith of the Philadelphia Inquirer .

Penn started off the program's second season under McCaffery 1-3, but are now on a win streak that extended to three straight games with Clark in attendance. The Quakers are next slated to play Friday against visiting Towson.

The Sixers recently strung together a five-game win streak of their own before dropping Monday's game against the Portland Trail Blazers.

Philadelphia, which will be missing Joel Embiid to illness, will look to get back on track in NBA Cup group stage action that marks the team's first game against Miami since the Heat acquired Giannis Antetokounmpo.

Defeating the Heat would allow the Sixers to remain in contention to win East Group B. Miami would advance to the NBA Cup quarterfinals by securing an eight straight victory.

articles.title: Lakers' Austin Reaves Says It 'Felt Like I Broke My Foot' Ahead of Return from Heel Injury
articles.summary: Austin Reaves seems to be working his way back for Friday's game against the San Antonio Spurs, but the Los Angeles Lakers guard had to overcome significant pain along the way.
articles.body:
Austin Reaves seems to be working his way back for Friday's game against the San Antonio Spurs, but the Los Angeles Lakers guard had to overcome significant pain along the way.

"I didn't think I broke my foot," he told reporters after practice Wednesday when discussing the heel contusion that has sidelined him since the Nov. 11 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks. "But it sure felt like I broke my foot."

He looks to be back, though, as head coach JJ Redick told reporters Reaves' practice was "the best I've ever seen him play. … I'm not joking."

The latest updates come after Redick said Monday he was "optimistic" Reaves would be able to take the court Friday.

That would be a significant boost for the Lakers. The 28-year-old is averaging 24.7 points, 4.7 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 51.3 percent from the field and 40.9 percent from deep this season.

If those numbers continued, he would set career-high marks in points per game and three-point shooting.

Reaves has assumed an even more important role in the Lakers' offense with LeBron James now on the Philadelphia 76ers. When healthy, he is the team's No. 2 option outside of Luka Dončić, and his presence helps alleviate some of the pressure from the primary playmaker.

He can hit from the outside when defenders collapse on Dončić or lead the offense when the NBA's scoring leader is on the bench.

To the Lakers' credit, they have continued to play well with Reaves sidelined. They are 4-1 in five games with players such as Walker Kessler and Matisse Thybulle providing sparks in bigger roles.

One of those wins came against the Charlotte Hornets when Quentin Grimes exploded for 47 points behind a sizzling 10-of-14 shooting from three-point range.

While the secondary players have helped keep the 15-3 Lakers near the top of the league standings, they ultimately need Reaves back if they are going to challenge the league's top teams come playoff time.

It is fitting, then, that his return could come against a Spurs team that is tied for the Western Conference's No. 1 seed at 15-3.

articles.title: LeBron James' 'Brilliance' Praised by Erik Spoelstra, 'He's Giving Father Time Hell' with 76ers
articles.summary: Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra remains impressed with Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James.
articles.body:
Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra remains impressed with Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James.

"I think what he's done here in this chapter is another form of brilliance," he told reporters ahead of his team's matchup with the Sixers on Wednesday. "Right now he's giving father time hell."

James, 41, has been excellent for the Sixers, averaging 16.6 points, 6.7 rebounds and 6.5 assists per game while embracing more of a playmaking role in a loaded lineup that also includes Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

He's been the perfect fit in that regard as the Sixers have raced out to a 14-4 start, erasing concerns about the team having too many cooks in the proverbial kitchen.

The season is long, of course, and the Sixers are still ironing out some of the kinks in their halfcourt offense. But in general, the James' addition has paid immediate dividends.

That will come as little surprise to Spoelstra, who coached the Big Three of James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh during the team's four trips to the NBA Finals and two titles in James' four seasons with the Heat.

Now he'll be tasked with slowing down James in a pivotal NBA Cup matchup between the teams. The Heat are currently atop Group B with a 2-0 record during the in-season tournament, while the Sixers are just behind them at 1-1. Philly will be without Joel Embiid in the contest due to illness .

articles.title: Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo ties program’s career points record
articles.summary: The accomplishments continue to pile up for senior Hannah Hidalgo after he tied the Notre Dame women's basketball career points record on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The feats continue to roll in for Notre Dame senior star guard Hannah Hidalgo this season.

The senior captain tied former Fighting Irish guard Arike Ogunbowale for the most career points in program history (2,626 points) , when Hidalgo scored 22 points in the 64-52 Battle 4 Atlantis win over Dayton on Tuesday.

Ogunbowale, who is currently a WNBA all-star for the Dallas Wing, played for Notre Dame in 2015-19 and was an All-American. She was also part of the Irish's national title season in 2017-18.

See the best photos from Notre Dame's 24-3 win over SMU

The recent accomplishment for Hidalgo came after she became the first college basketball player to reach 2,500 points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists and 500 steals in her career .

Hidalgo will have an opportunity to break the career points record on Thursday when USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll No. 12 Notre Dame (6-0) faces No. 22 West Virginia in the Battle 4 Atlantis.

Through six games, Hidalgo is averaging 27.7 points and is shooting 53.4% from the field and 92.5% from the free-throw line.

articles.title: SEC adds LSU men's basketball coach Will Wade to lawsuit as expulsion vote looms
articles.summary: The Southeastern Conference has added LSU men's basketball coach Will Wade to a lawsuit the league has filed to assert its ability to expel the school.
articles.body:
The SEC has filed an amended complaint adding LSU men's basketball coach Will Wade to its federal lawsuit asserting the authority to expel the school as a member.

Wade joins several LSU administrators and coaches already named in the lawsuit, including university president Wade Rousse, athletics director Verge Ausberry and football coach Lane Kiffin. Also named is Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill.

The amendment was filed "because the additional allegations reflect and relate to events that have occurred since the SEC filed its First Amended Complaint on Sept. 8, 2026," the supplemental complaint reads.

The conference has scheduled a vote of all 16 member schools for Dec. 3 "to consider the termination of LSU's membership in the SEC." To go into effect, at least two-thirds of members are required to vote in favor of LSU's dismissal.

This expulsion vote was triggered in part by the basketball program's decision to roster and play former All-America guard RJ Luis Jr ., who went undrafted after leaving St. John's in 2025 and spent last season with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics, never appearing in an NBA regular-season game.

Luis signed with Wade and LSU in May and was granted a preliminary injunction that declared him eligible for the 2026-27 season. He made his debut on Nov. 18, scoring 11 points against Louisiana-Monroe. A day later, Rousse ordered Wade to remove Luis from the roster .

In an affidavit, SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey said that both Wade and Ausberry had said they would not play Luis.

"LSU's decision to play RJ Luis Jr. weeks after telling the court it was 'demonstrably false' that it would violate the rules hands the SEC its best evidence yet," Ryan Regula, a partner at Snell & Wilmer who works extensively with colleges and universities among his specialties, told USA TODAY Sports. "It also significantly undercuts LSU's position that the case is moot."

Next week's vote marks the second time in several months the SEC has openly discussed LSU's future in the conference .

In September, the conference and LSU were in dispute over Kiffin's wish to add to the Tigers' roster several former Power Four players who had spent the summer in NFL training camps.

A month earlier, the SEC had passed a new rule prohibiting the rostering of athletes who had signed a contract with an NFL, NBA or WNBA team (or minor-league affiliate) or been listed on a professional roster.

The SEC considered a vote on the school's membership but backed away after Kiffin and the football program backed off rostering the former college players, many of whom had been filed lawsuits to gain a season of eligibility in the wake of the NCAA's move to a five-for-five eligibility model.

"This thing is in litigation," Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana said on Wednesday. "We're going to leave it up to the lawyers. We're going to let LSU make those particular statements. So we'll just wait and see what happens and there will be decisions and comments made by the LSU leadership."

"Again, as we continue on this unfortunate path, we'll unfortunately have to leave it in the hands of the lawyers."

articles.title: Historic first quarter powers No. 2 Michigan to blowout win over Toledo
articles.summary: Logging its second-highest scoring quarter in program history, No. 2 Michigan Women’s Basketball took down Toledo 102-56
articles.body:
If there is one thing the No. 2 Michigan women's basketball team will do, it's light up the scoreboard. No matter who the opponent is, the Wolverines' offense is a machine that never stops churning, and their matchup against Toledo in the Bahamas at the Baha Mar Pink Flamingo Championship was no exception.

Powered by its second-best quarter in program history, Michigan (7-0) put away the Rockets (4-3) with ease. The Wolverines scored at every level, draining threes and powering through contested layups against a potent Toledo defense. The result was five players ending up scoring in the double digits and a commanding 102-56 victory.

Michigan's record-breaking 36-point first quarter was characterized by its combination of aggression and pinpoint accuracy, shooting 70 percent and 71.4 percent from three. The Wolverines took control of the tempo of the game right away, speeding up the Rockets to give them no time to apply any semblance of defensive pressure.

Junior guard Kendall Dudley led the charge, shooting a perfect 5-for-5 in the quarter and tallying 11 points. She consistently used her size and swiftness to drive to the rim and tip in easy layups. With a point total of 10, junior guard Olivia Olson was closely behind Dudley in offensive contributions, making her own magic by grabbing boards, ripping steals and forcing a foul.

In the first quarter, Toledo certainly offered the path of least resistance for Michigan's assertive offense, giving the Wolverines wide-open looks and putting them up, 36-15. But the Rockets weren't going down without a fight.

Toledo looked like a different team entirely on the defensive end and went back to its bread and butter of active and communicative defense. The easy looks of the first half vanished as the Rockets' sticky man coverage stuck a wrench in Michigan's offensive game plan. On the offensive end, Toledo slowed down possessions, finding the perfect chances it needed to attempt to cut the deficit.

Still, the Wolverines didn't stay down long. Michigan consistently punished the Rockets for any misfires, bullying its way for rebounds and subsequently converting on the possessions. Junior guard Te'Yala Delfosse was the maestro behind the offensive fire the Wolverines did conjure up, consistently knocking down contested shots from all over the floor. Toledo just about outscored Michigan 19-18 in the quarter, but the Rockets' best wasn't nearly enough to change the tide of the game, with the Wolverines still up 54-34.

And once the second half began, it was clear that there was no more weathering the storm for Toledo. Michigan's defense upped the ante to begin the third quarter, giving the Rockets no easy shots and taking complete control of the glass to limit them to one-and-dones. The Wolverines went on a 16-2 run over the first four minutes, fueled by their dominance in the paint, ballooning their lead up to an untouchable 34.

By the fourth quarter, Michigan's 40+ point cushion allowed it to rotate its bench in at no cost. And they only packed on to the pummeling, limiting Toledo to just six points all quarter.

The Wolverines now leave Bahama still perfect, and they showed the Rockets exactly why their record is so unblemished. Their offense never took its foot off the gas for long, sealing the game in its usual assertive fashion.

articles.title: If Warriors want to trade Kristaps Porzingis by December 16, who are potential partners, targets?
articles.summary: Explaining the "re-aggregation" deadline in the Golden State's attempt to trade Kristaps Porzingis, examining potential teams the Warriors could match up wit...
articles.body:
Before the world turned in the Bay Area, before the biggest swing of Mike Dunleavy 's tenure as general manager of the Golden State Warriors , he laid a stepping stone on Dec. 15, 2024. In came Schröder, a veteran who - at the time - gave the Warriors obviously-needed guard. But that fit was so rough that Golden State jettisoned Schröder as part of the Jimmy Butler trade just two months later. A new era was born .

But the Warriors would never actually be sitting here with Butler, two years later, if they hadn't traded for Schröder on the exact day they did.

This remains one of the most prominent examples of the modern NBA's "re-aggregation rule" - and a blueprint for the Warriors' current best-case scenario with Kristaps Porzingis . Under the league's collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a player traded before Dec. 16 can be used as part of a potential future trade to match salaries in a deal at February's trade deadline. And Golden State specifically planned for this with Schröder, whose former $13 million contract the organization acquired and then packaged as part of the eventual Feb. 2025 deal for Butler.

The Warriors, now, will have an incentive to find a deal for Porzingis before Dec. 16 for the same reasons. If they're able to find a trade partner, a smaller fish acquired in a salary-match with Porzingis could be packaged for a bigger fish in February - and theoretically then have more trade value than Porzingis, a player who may never see a basketball court again.

The issue, of course, remains Porzingis's current lack of any tangible trade value beyond his semi-expiring contract. Teams are much more likely to want to move off a bad contract in February than they are in December, so early in the season. A team source previously told the Chronicle earlier in November that Golden State will look at all options but wouldn't force a deal solely for better bargaining power by the re-aggregation deadline.

"I definitely think they have a chance to move him, just a matter of their level of urgency to do so," a league personnel source told the Chronicle, asked whether Golden State could find a partner for Porzingis by Dec. 16. "Might be easier when teams know their direction and just want the contract and talk buyout."

Swinging a move for Porzingis before that deadline, though, would allow the Warriors to add immediate help - perhaps another center to pair with the ascending Charles Bassey , perhaps another offensive creator - while building out a package for a major target in February. Anthony Davis, now with the Wizards, remains a clear game-changing option, who the Warriors could land by aggregating salaries with a combination of Porzingis (or a December acquisition in his place), Draymond Green and Moses Moody .

For now, here's a look around the NBA at four potential December swings for Golden State, and the Porzingis-laid financial path it would take for the Warriors to land them.

Total contract: Unrestricted free agent in 2030-31, $25 million average salary

Reid is a good player having a bad season with a bad contract, which could land directly in Golden State's Porzingis-holding wheelhouse. After years in Minnesota thriving as one of the best sixth men in the NBA, a trade to Charlotte (in the LaMelo Ball deal) in July hasn't been kind to Reid, who's averaging 17.7 points on 17.5 shots per game and was benched at halftime in one game early this season .

Reid isn't the rim protector that the Warriors originally coveted with Porzingis, but he'd bring a similar effect offensively. He's a 6-foot-9 center who has shot 38% from three on 5.7 attempts per game across the past four seasons, and could be a dynamic offensive weapon who would allow Golden State to lean fully into its five-out offensive concept.

Simplest path to a deal: Package Porzingis with a bench player like De'Anthony Melton (who becomes trade-eligible Dec. 15) or Gui Santos and then add a couple draft picks, depending on Charlotte's asking price.

Comment from the league personnel source: "Contract looks tough to have now, and think Charlotte would want multiple assets as he's been bad but LaMelo has been good so for optics (sic)."

Total contract: Unrestricted free agent in 2029-30, $27.2 million average salary

The 30-year-old Turner is averaging 6.3 rebounds and 8.3 points on 38% shooting in 26.8 minutes per game. He was a key contributor on a Pacers team that nearly won the NBA Finals in 2024-25, but has looked lost in Milwaukee the past two seasons. The Bucks would likely want to get out of Turner's contract, but would the Warriors value Turner enough to absorb his salary the next few seasons? Doubtful.

Simplest path to a deal: Package Porzingis with Moody. That would bring little value from the Warriors' perspective, though.

Total contract remaining: Unrestricted free agent in 2029-30, $18.1 million average salary

The 28-year-old Gafford has been a solid contributor in Dallas for years now, and would give Golden State rim protection (1.6 blocks in 22.1 minutes per game) while allowing Draymond Green to comfortably play power forward. Gafford is a lob threat and capable facilitator and could form an intriguing center tandem with a similar player in Bassey.

Trade Porzingis straight up and add some kind of draft capital. This would depend if Dallas wanted to clear future money off its books.

Comment from the league personnel source: "Gafford is good and on a good contract, would be an interesting target."

Total contract: Unrestricted free agent in 2029-30, $28 million average salary

Perhaps no player in the NBA - besides the LeBron James/Anthony Davis rumors in the summer - has been more heavily linked to Golden State since last season than Murphy, a 6-foot-8 sharpshooter who averaged 21.5 points per game last season. While dealing with knee troubles this season, though, Murphy has dropped to 15.1 points per game on a lost Pelicans team.

Package Porzingis, Moody and draft capital for Murphy, who would have league-wide interest if he's truly on the trade block and would likely command a significantly higher asking price.

Comment from the league personnel source: "Trey is a whole other level of swing, good pairing with Yaxel for the future of the team as well, would cost multiple firsts. ... If I'm GS, I would part with picks for Trey."

articles.title: Charlotte Hornets jersey history No. 9 Aaron Harrison 2015-2017
articles.summary: After two seasons at Kentucky, Aaron Harrison performed well enough in the summer league to earn a contract from the Charlotte Hornets.
articles.body:
Unlike his twin brother, Andrew Harrison, who was taken in the second-round of the 2015 NBA Draft, Aaron Harrison went undrafted. That said, Aaron played well enough during the NBA Summer League with the Hornets to earn Charlotte's final roster spot. From there, the former Kentucky Wildcats guard played two seasons with the Hornets, averaging 0.7 points, 0.7 rebounds, 0.2 assists and 0.2 steals in only 4.2 minutes per game. After five games during the 2016-17 season, the Hornets waived Harrison.

He would go on to sign with the Dallas Mavericks for the 2017-18 season, playing nine games and making three starts in what would turn out to be his final NBA season. Following his stint in the NBA, Harrison pursued a professional career overseas. At 32 years old, Harrison is currently a free agent.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton Says Pacers Are 'Protecting Me From Myself' amid Hamstring Injury Rehab
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton has missed 14 straight games due to a left hamstring strain.
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton has missed 14 straight games due to a left hamstring strain .

On Wednesday, Haliburton admitted that the organization is "protecting me from myself" as he looks to return to the court.

"Being completely honest, the organization is doing as best they can of protecting me from myself," he said. "Obviously you guys know, I'm a competitor. I play through injuries more than a lot of guys, and that's just who I am. Unfortunately, I am banged up a lot, but I play as much as I can."

Haliburton missed all of 2025-26 with a torn Achilles suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. He had just embarked on a remarkable playoff run, hitting clutch shot after clutch shot to help lead the Pacers to one win away from the NBA championship.

Thankfully, Haliburton was able to return for the beginning of this season. He fared quite well to start, averaging 21.8 points on 51.6 percent shooting and 9.5 assists per game over four contests.

Unfortunately, Haliburton has now been out for about a month. However, his return appears imminent, which is a welcome sight for a 6-12 Pacers squad. Haliburton said in the first-ever "Notes From Zero" episode , which was posted on Sunday, that he wants to be back before the beginning of December.

"I just want to be healthy," Haliburton said. "I'm healing well though. The goal for me is to be back before the start of December."

On Tuesday, Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle had this to say on Indianapolis' 107.5 The Fan if Haliburton could return for the team's back-to-back set on Friday and Saturday vs. the Philadelphia 76ers and at the Chicago Bulls, respectively.

"Well, as we used to say when I was in TV, stay tuned," Carlisle said (h/t James Boyd of The Athletic).

So fans will stay tuned hoping Haliburton gets back by the end of the week. If not, his next chance to play will be on Tuesday at the Cleveland Cavaliers.
